title: Single Lever Faucet vs Dual Lever Faucet: Which One Should You Choose?
metaTitle: Single vs Dual Lever Faucet: Which Is Better?
description: Compare single and dual lever faucets in terms of style, control, and efficiency. Find out which faucet type is best for your bathroom or kitchen today.
bannerAlt: Single Lever Faucet vs Dual Lever Faucet
bodyHtml:
When designing or upgrading your kitchen or bathroom, one of the most essential yet often overlooked elements is the faucet. Aesthetics, ease of use, water control, and long-term durability — all come into play when selecting the right faucet. Among the most common choices are Single Lever Faucets and Dual Lever Faucets.

But which one should you choose?

In this blog, we’ll break down the key differences between the two types, explore their pros and cons, and help you make an informed decision — with insights from Prayag, India’s most trusted faucet manufacturer.

What Is a Single Lever Faucet?

A Single Lever Faucet has one handle that controls both water flow and temperature. By lifting and turning the lever, users can easily adjust the mix of hot and cold water.

Advantages:

  • Ease of Use: Simple one-handed operation — great for kids, elderly, and busy kitchens.

  • Sleek Design: Minimalistic and modern appearance suits contemporary spaces.

  • Space-Saving: Ideal for compact sinks or wall-mounted installations.

  • Quick Installation: Fewer parts and easier plumbing.

Limitations:

  • Less Precise Temperature Control: Slight adjustments might be needed for the perfect balance.

  • If the Valve Fails: You lose both hot and cold water control.

What Is a Dual Lever Faucet?

A Dual Lever Faucet comes with two separate handles — one for hot water and the other for cold. You mix the temperature manually by adjusting both levers.

Advantages:

  • Better Temperature Precision: You have direct control over each water source.

  • Classic Aesthetic: Preferred for traditional and vintage bathroom styles.

  • Separate Shut-off: Even if one valve fails, the other can still function.

Limitations:

  • Two-Handed Operation: Not as convenient, especially when multitasking.

  • Takes More Space: Not ideal for smaller sinks or countertops.

  • Slightly Longer Installation: More parts = more fittings = more time.

Design & Aesthetic Considerations

Functionality & Performance

Which Faucet is Better for You?

Choose Single Lever Faucet if:

  • You want convenience and speed

  • You have a modern, minimalist design theme

  • You’re installing in a compact space

Choose Dual Lever Faucet if:

  • You value temperature precision

  • Your home has a classic or traditional decor

  • You don’t mind using both hands or want separate hot/cold controls

Final Thoughts

Both single lever and dual lever faucets have their strengths — and the best choice depends on your personal preferences, usage, and style goals. While single lever faucets offer ease and elegance, dual lever faucets deliver control and character.
